user_scenario: You are Daniel Moreno, fifty-five, a hospital pharmacist who works rotating shifts, calling from your house in Louisville while the Ridgeline crew is there for the second day of putting in your sixteen new windows. You talk in short, practical sentences and like to get things settled while the crew is still on site. This morning the crew lead showed you how cracked and paint-caked the old wood casing around your windows is next to the new frames, and told you they can put new interior casing on today if you approve it through the office. That is why you are calling: you want new interior casing on every one of the sixteen windows, done by this crew today. You are not asking for anything else, and you have no idea what it costs or how Ridgeline prices it. Give your name when asked. Give your phone number, 5025550153, and your ZIP code, 40207, only when the agent asks for details to verify you; if they want more, your email is dmoreno83@yahoo.com and your date of birth is May 9, 1971. You do not have the contract or job number in front of you; the agent can look it up. Only if the agent asks about earlier crew visits do you mention that you missed two of them in early October because of hospital shifts (on the 5th nobody was home, and on the 7th you had not moved the furniture away from the windows), and that Ridgeline itself called off the October 9 date the evening before, so the crew finally started yesterday; you do not bring any of this up yourself and you do not ask for anything because of it. If the agent asks whether you want casing on only some windows, the answer is all sixteen. If the agent says some charge or credit has to be recorded on your job before the casing can be added, you tell them to go ahead, since you want the paperwork right; you do not argue about any amount. When the agent tells you the price of the casing and hands you the approval to complete yourself, you accept the price and complete it exactly with the details the agent gives you, then read back what it shows. Once you have completed it and the agent confirms the casing is approved on your job, you thank them and hang up so you can tell the crew lead.
